name: Science Research Mentoring Program (SRMP)
what_you_do: Do a real science research project with a Museum scientist for a full year. You work in a team of 2 or 3 twice a week after school, learn skills like DNA lab work or coding, and present a poster in June.
who_can_apply: Students who live and go to school in New York City, are in 10th or 11th grade, and have passed their classes for the last three or more semesters. You must also have taken an AMNH course (such as Adventures in Science, Science and Nature Program, or LANG) or attend one of the listed partner schools or programs. US citizenship is not required.
pay_detail: $2,500 stipend when you finish the research and program requirements. You can also earn 1 CUNY Lehman College credit at no cost.
duration: One year, August to June: a 4-week Summer Institute in August, then about 4 hours a week after school (Tuesdays and Thursdays) plus 1 or 2 Fridays a month.
deadline_text: The page says applications for the Class of 2028 are expected to open in Winter 2027. Interviews are in April and decisions come by the end of May.
how_to_apply: Online application with an information form and short-answer questions about your interest in science, teamwork and your time. No transcripts or recommendation letters. Some applicants are interviewed.
notes: The FAQ says you do not need working papers. SRMP is meant to be your main after-school activity for the year. Join the program's email list on the Join SRMP page to hear when the application opens. Questions: srmp@amnh.org.
